name: Sephatiah
overview: Sephatiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Jehoshaphat. The biblical record provides limited information about him beyond his lineage, emphasizing his familial connection within the royal line of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Sephatiah means 'YHWH has judged,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's sovereign judgment. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 21:2 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Sephatiah is explicitly recorded as the son of Jehoshaphat, situating him within the royal family of Judah. Additionally, it is inferred from the same biblical passage that he was killed by Jehoram, suggesting a tragic end linked to the political and familial turmoil of that era.
scriptureSignificance: Sephatiah's significance in Scripture is primarily tied to his royal lineage as the son of Jehoshaphat, a king of Judah. His mention alongside the violent actions of Jehoram highlights the instability and divine judgment upon the royal family during that period. Though not extensively detailed, Sephatiah's life reflects the biblical themes of God's sovereignty and judgment within the monarchy of Judah.
